scope: Every26 explicit required-property/HSM/atomic-commit bullet in plan4.1,4.4,7.2, individually mapped to current implementation and actual passing stable/MSRV CI tests. This is a scoped contract audit, not all normative plan prose or release qualification. User callback purity and authenticated sources remain consumer obligations; finite fixtures do not prove all executions.

items.requirement: All state changes are returned as a candidate value, never by mutating the published state.
items.assessment: Native owner exposes immutable state and evaluates an owned candidate; preparation/drop does not change the published tuple.

items.requirement: A guard refusal is a typed result. `Unhandled` means no handler accepted the event; it is **not** the same as `Rejected` or an execution error.
items.assessment: Business rejection, unhandled fallback and concrete model errors retain separate enum/result variants.

items.requirement: Tentative effects produced before a rejection/error are dropped; they never reach the authoritative outbox.
items.assessment: Staging is private to the attempt, including ignored errors and caught payload-destructor panic; refusal/error drops it.

items.requirement: `Machine::transition` has no blanket `Clone`, `Serialize`, `Send`, `Sync`, `std`, or `alloc` bound. Concrete storage profiles add only their necessary bounds.
items.assessment: The base trait has no Clone/Serde/Send/Sync or allocator bound. The concrete non-Clone fixture compiles/runs; allocation-free profiles have separate allocator-probe evidence.

items.requirement: A successful `Transition` does not mean it is committed. A `PreparedTransition`/`ReadyTransition` token binds the expected head and the exact candidate; only the machine owner or durable store may publish it.
items.assessment: Exclusive borrow-bound prepared handle is consumed on local publication; durable preparation verifies exact receipt coordinates before publishing.

items.requirement: `MemoryMachine::handle` owns published state and swaps it only after all validation succeeds. Reading state is borrowing, not exposing mutable references that bypass transitions.
items.assessment: Owner validates then publishes state/head/provenance/intents coherently, with retired destructors run after the tuple changes; read returns no mutable state reference.

items.requirement: Keep source error types precise; use typed `thiserror` wrappers for infrastructure failures, preserving application errors in generic variants.
items.assessment: MachineFailure and hosted preparation wrappers retain concrete application/codec errors rather than erasing them to strings.

items.requirement: A finite active leaf path and explicitly declared parents/superstates.
items.assessment: A single active leaf maps through explicit parents into bounded inline StatePath storage; no runtime registry.

items.requirement: Event dispatch from the active leaf outward through parent handlers until handled or explicitly rejected.
items.assessment: Selection visits leaf then parents in declared order; the oracle checks dispatch and LCA action order.

items.requirement: Distinguish **unhandled** (can bubble) from **rejected** (terminal refusal).
items.assessment: Only Unhandled bubbles. Rejection and typed evaluation faults stop selection.

items.requirement: Guards evaluated for the chosen transition; no side effects in guards.
items.assessment: select receives immutable inputs and no sink. Deterministic/pure user predicates remain a documented consumer obligation; Rust cannot prevent arbitrary user I/O.

items.requirement: Deterministic exit actions from leaf to least common ancestor; transition action; entry actions from ancestor to target leaf. Exact self-transition/internal-transition semantics must be specified and tested.
items.assessment: External transitions exit active leaf to LCA, run action, then enter target path; external self reenters and internal retains the leaf.

items.requirement: Entry/exit *effects* are staged intents, never executed during evaluation. If any stage fails, the complete candidate is discarded.
items.assessment: Hook intents are staged in the native attempt and any failure discards candidate and all prior hooks; ignored sink errors stop later hooks.

items.requirement: Stable typed state/transition identifiers for provenance (not user-authored string IDs); an enum-based `StatePath` interface may provide the relationship. Avoid runtime reflection requirements.
items.assessment: Typed Copy+Eq nodes and typed TransitionId supply stable model-owned identities. Definition pinning is a host/model contract; strings are not reflection keys.

items.requirement: Cycles and repeated events are permitted but bounded by the caller's per-dispatch depth/step/intent budgets; no accidental infinite implicit transition loops.
items.assessment: Finite paths refuse repeated parent nodes/depth overflow, while repeated event dispatch and cyclic transition tables remain allowed under per-attempt intent limits. There are no implicit completion loops.

items.requirement: No orthogonal/parallel regions in 0.5.0; this must be explicit in docs rather than pretending nesting covers all Statig HSM features.
items.assessment: The public HierarchyModel contract explicitly excludes orthogonal regions. This is a deliberate supported-profile limit, not a claim of all HSM semantics.

items.requirement: Check the exact machine scope and pinned model/schema fingerprint.
items.assessment: Host authorization precedes scoped access; transaction admission pins exact complete scope and definition/schema.

items.requirement: Validate the expected revision/CAS and event uniqueness under the transaction lock.
items.assessment: Read-only preflight may resolve old work, but new commits revalidate under immediate transaction lock. Independent workers compete against one predecessor.

items.requirement: If the same event ID and same immutable payload/commit identity already exist, return a verifiably identical duplicate receipt, not an additional transition.
items.assessment: Exact old event/content is resolved before predecessor CAS and returns the original complete-batch receipt.

items.requirement: If the same ID exists with different content, reject with conflict. Never treat it as idempotent.
items.assessment: Same event ID with different immutable content is conflict, not a duplicate success.

items.requirement: Atomically commit accepted event, new revision/head and state identity, replay payload/storage references as required, and **all** outgoing intent records. All-or-nothing.
items.assessment: Event/record/intent/head/usage writes share one transaction; silent suppressed writes, later intent conflicts and post-write corruption roll back.

items.requirement: A rejected/unhandled evaluation must not call the transition-commit path as though it succeeded.
items.assessment: Only accepted native preparation can construct the private admission batch. Rejected/unhandled outcomes retain no commit batch.

items.requirement: Ensure a crash after commit and before receipt can be resolved by reading authoritative persisted records, not by guessing whether the action succeeded.
items.assessment: Actual SIGKILL boundaries include commit-before-receipt; reopening and exact retry resolve all-or-nothing accepted history. This is process-death evidence, not arbitrary hardware power-loss proof.

items.requirement: Never dispatch an effect before the **verifiable committed receipt** and authorization checks.
items.assessment: Preparation and the outbox never dispatch effects. Source authorization and trusted native receiver verification gate handoff/ACK; private preparation verifies the full commit receipt before local publication. External execution remains under native task/saga/host authority.

items.requirement: Enforce scoped quotas, record-size limits, history retention, resource bounds, and integer overflow prevention before irreversible partial mutation.
items.assessment: Staging/wire/payload bounds and journal/delivery scoped quotas preflight mutations with checked arithmetic; history is append-only and refuses overflow rather than evicting dedupe or uncertain work.

items.requirement: Preserve a coherent read of state/head/event for concurrent readers; a state-byte payload and the revision that describes it cannot become independently visible.
items.assessment: Snapshot reads verify one coherent head/state/event tuple under a read transaction; competing reader/writer test checks no mixed tuple is returned.

remaining: Audit remaining detailed prose/clauses outside these26 bullets using the existing phase, test-layer, invariant, compatibility and maintenance audits without assuming those scopes close the entire plan.
Complete current-source full campaign and supplementary fuzz, resolve retained performance findings, reconcile final artifacts and dated release notes.
Historical baseline/compile-fixture sequencing remains explicitly unproven; later passing observations are not rewritten as prior completion.
